newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday urged unionists to participate in talks getting under way today between the government, union and employers that will look at ways to reform the job market. Simitis said he wanted unionists to come to the table without preconceived notions and that the aim was to provide relief for the unemployed.

--A difference on opinion in Paris yesterday - where European foreign and defence ministers are meeting - between Turkey and the Dutch EU presidency, who say Greek and Turkish experts should meet, and Greece, whose Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said he preferred "a written procedure because it helps when it comes to keeping commitments".

--The much-awaited 12th volume of the archives of former president of the republic Constantine Karamanlis will be officially launched tonight. The final volume of Karamanlis's papers contains pointed references to the late founder and president of ruling party PASOK Andreas Papandreou and to Karamanlis's successor at the helm of conservative opposition New Democracy Constantine Mitsotakis.

--PASOK cadres were scathing yesterday of Karamanlis's references to Papandreou and reports say Simitis will not be present at the official launch. Mitsotakis is also reported to be planning to put in a non-appearance.
--Conservative opposition New Democracy's recent jibes at the ruling party over the failure to come up with proposals to revise the constitution has forced the government's hand.

--There's friction between the municipality of Athens and the public order minister after the city placed 150 parking meters in non-parking areas. Minister George Romeos said the municipality's move placed the safety of drivers at risk and worsened traffic circulation problems in the capital.

--Police are warning the public to be on guard following the death of a young student knifed in a central park while with his girlfriend. Police say there have been a number of senseless attacks in the city's six parks recently. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4'
